rationale_overall: Filtered out a large volume of non-investable noise this week: private companies with no public ticker (SpaceX Starship/Gen2 sat cap, OpenAI training report, OrbitAid, Saildrone), foreign/government launch programs with no US-listed pure-play (ISRO PSLV-C62 failure, China satellite launch, India Pinaka rocket exports, NASA Artemis II rollout), war/geopolitical event coverage with no ticker attached (Russia-Ukraine hypersonic/drone strikes, Iran protests, OSCE missile discussion), and outright keyword false-matches (a hockey team called the 'Rocket', a 'rocket attack' assault charge in Belfast). Generic thematic listicles (best robotics stocks, best quantum computing stocks, AI chip stock 'not Nvidia') named no specific tickers I could act on. The one item worth flagging is the DoD's reported $1B equity stake in L3Harris's missile solutions unit (satnews.com), a concrete defense/rearmament catalyst that would fit the profile's geopolitical-realignment wave and is currently unrepresented in the watchlist — but it comes from a single trade-press outlet with no corroboration from a major financial source, and the current holdings show no offsetting fundamental breach this week (RKLB's 'soaring 174%, still a buy?' piece and 1.5% dip, SMR's 2.3% dip/'time to sell?' clickbait, and a Huawei-competition note on NVDA are all noise-level, not thesis-breaking). Per the swap discipline for this cadence, a single uncorroborated article is not enough to displace a core wave holding, so the watchlist is unchanged this week.
